answer: Each identity must seal a unique piece of data and periodically prove it still holds a distinct copy, so one operator with a thousand identities must store a thousand genuinely different sealed sectors rather than pointing the same cheap disk at a thousand names. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. The walnut is the sealed sector, the tundra the replication challenge that proves it is still unique, and the hollow the identity the sealed data is bound to; cloning the walnut fails the tundra, and one sector cannot satisfy two hollow bindings.
